Hi Michael — great question and thanks for the RFP. High level answers up front, with a short note on tradeoffs:

- Term discounts: we can provide a multi-year effective discount that increases with total committed $ (e.g., 10–18% range for a 3-year commitment depending on upfront vs annual prepay mix).
- Refunds / early termination: common approaches are (A) straight amortization of prepaid amounts over the committed term with pro-rata refunds less a short termination fee, (B) holdback escrow to cover potential clawbacks, or (C) tiered refund schedule (higher refunds early, ramping down after year 1).
- Co-terming: we support co-terming but it affects effective economics — to co-term we typically pro-rate remaining prepaid value to align with the new co-term end date (or offer a structured credit).

I can put a concise matrix together with numerical examples and an offer we can present to procurement. Quick ask: who from your legal/procurement should I include when I send a draft?

I'll follow up tomorrow with a proposal matrix and a recommended compromise that balances your flexibility needs and our pricing risk.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Asterion's redlines (attached). They want a clear formulaic refund and prefer a shorter amortization window if possible. Procurement will argue to minimize escrow/holdback language.

Options I'm thinking we can position (preferred -> concession):
1) Preferred: 36-month commitment with Year 1 75–100% upfront (15% effective discount), Years 2–3 annual prepay with 12-month amortization on early termination; termination fee equal to 10% of remaining prepaid value. Smooth economics and limited exposure.
2) Compromise: 36-month commitment with Year 1 50% upfront (12% discount), Years 2–3 annual prepay, 18-month amortization window for refunds, termination fee 5% + reasonable admin fee.
3) Concession: 36-month commitment with annual prepay only and 24–36 month amortization (lower discounts).

Tradeoffs: shorter amortization = higher upfront refund risk for us; if we accept 12-month amortization we should tighten churn definitions (what constitutes termination) and require 30 days notice. Also want to avoid a broad escrow structure — prefer a formulaic refund plus small termination fee.

Attached: proposed_term_matrix.xlsx (stub) — contains sample numerics across the three options. Can you please: Marissa — sanity-check discount ranges and termination fee. Rishi — confirm whether legal is ok with 12-month amortization with the churn/notice language, or if we should insist on 18 months. Monica — ops question: if we accept 12-month amortization, how do we cap capacity exposure / guarantee reallocation?

Thanks — planning to turn this into a customer-facing offer by EOD Friday.

— Diego

Michael / Sara — thanks for the redlines and the clarity on procurement's priorities. Based on internal alignment, below is a concise offer and the mechanics we recommend (aimed at being procurement-friendly while protecting Redwood's economics).

Offer (36-month commitment):
- Pricing: Year 1 prepay 50% of committed ARR at signing — 14% effective term discount on year 1 spend. Years 2 & 3 billed as annual prepay (paid up front at start of each year) with a 10% discount on those year payments. Net blended term discount ~13%.

Refund / Early Termination Mechanics (formulaic):
- Prepaid amounts are amortized on a monthly straight-line basis over the remaining committed months.
- Customer may terminate with 30 days notice. Refund = Unamortized prepaid balance less a termination fee equal to 7.5% of the unamortized balance and any unpaid usage through termination date.
- Alternative shorter amortization: for use-cases where Asterion requires a 12-month guaranteed refund window, we can accept 12-month amortization for Year 1 only, in exchange for an increased termination fee of 12% and a minimum 6-month notice for that provision.

Co-terming / Vendor consolidation:
- If customer elects to co-term with an existing vendor within 180 days of signature, Redwood will provide a pro-rated credit equal to the unamortized prepaid value, applied toward a co-term invoice or refunded per the formula above. For consolidations that materially reduce committed consumption, Redwood reserves the right to re-evaluate unit pricing for the remaining term (standard protective clause).

Next steps:
1) I've attached an offer PDF (RDW_offer_Asterion_v2.pdf) with the numerical matrix for the three prepay mixes you requested.
2) If this looks acceptable, we'll prepare a narrow amendment that articulates the refund formula and termination fee (to avoid open-ended escrow language).
3) If procurement wants the 12-month amortization for Year 1, confirm in writing and we'll submit the adjusted DocuSign for signature (link included).
